guide.summary: Churches, concert halls, national and city museums, family attractions and a city pool, with bakeries, cafés, dinners and bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Matur og Drykkur opens only Wednesday to Sunday from 18:00, so plan a Monday or Tuesday dinner elsewhere, such as Grillmarkaðurinn, which seats from 17:30 every day.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The National Museum of Iceland, the National Gallery of Iceland and Whales of Iceland all publish daily hours, while Matur og Drykkur opens only Wednesday to Sunday. Harpa stays open until 20:00 from Wednesday to Saturday and until 18:00 on other days.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Grillmarkaðurinn, Fiskmarkaðurinn and Snaps take table bookings through Dineout. FlyOver Iceland lists 5,690 ISK online against 6,250 ISK at the gate.

toolkit.label: Walk-in only
toolkit.copy: Café Loki states first come, first served with no table reservations. Kaldi Bar takes neither table nor group bookings.

toolkit.label: Age and height rules
toolkit.copy: Kaldi Bar has an age limit of 22. FlyOver Iceland requires children to be at least 100cm tall, and children 13 and under must be accompanied by someone 14 or older.

guide.dek: Base yourself in the centre, book dinners a few days ahead, and save the museums for the darker afternoons since most keep daily daytime hours.
intro: Reykjavík's centre is compact, and Hallgrímskirkja on Hallgrímstorg is the clearest anchor. Its summer notice gave daily hours of 10:00 to 20:00 from 20 May 2026, with tower access closing at 19:45, so check its current hours; it also warns that access can be limited during services, ceremonies and concerts. Down at the waterfront, Harpa on Austurbakki opens Sunday to Tuesday from 10:00 to 18:00 and Wednesday to Saturday until 20:00, and its box office stays open longer on event nights. Perlan on Öskjuhlíð runs its exhibitions from 9:00 to 21:00, with a bar open until 21:00.

For a museum day, the National Museum of Iceland at Suðurgata 41 opens daily from 10:00 to 17:00, charges adults 3,300 ISK and lets under-18s in free. Its exhibition on the bridal costume runs until 9 May 2027. The National Gallery of Iceland at Laufásvegur 12 also opens every day from 10am to 5pm, with "Kjarval in the East" until 17 January 2027 and a show of Ukrainian icons until 17 October 2027. Reykjavík Art Museum spreads across three buildings: Hafnarhús on Tryggvagata stays open until 22:00 on Thursdays, while Kjarvalsstaðir and Ásmundarsafn keep daytime hours.

Eating out rewards a little planning. Grillmarkaðurinn, Fiskmarkaðurinn and Snaps take bookings through Dineout, and Matur og Drykkur on Mýrargata opens only Wednesday to Sunday from 18:00, with its food-and-drink menu listed at 24,500 ISK and no vegan, gluten-free or lactose-free menu. Café Loki, across the street from Hallgrímskirkja, takes no table reservations and serves Icelandic rye bread plates from 8am. For an early start, Brauð & Co on Frakkastígur opens at 06:30, Sandholt on Laugavegur at 07:30 and Mokka on Skólavörðustígur at 9:00.

In the evening, Kaldi Bar at Laugavegur 20b has an age limit of 22, takes no table or group bookings and runs a daily happy hour from 16:00 to 19:00 on draught beer and wine. Slippbarinn on Mýrargata has happy hour every day from 15:00 to 18:00. If you are travelling with children, the Family Park and Zoo at Múlavegur 2 opens daily from 10:00 to 17:00 with free entry for under-sixes, Whales of Iceland on Fiskislóð is open every day of the year, and FlyOver Iceland requires riders to be at least 100cm tall.
summaryCards: Pair Hallgrímskirkja, which posts its tower hours on its own site, with Harpa on the waterfront and the National Museum of Iceland on Suðurgata.
Start with a pastry at Brauð & Co on Frakkastígur from 06:30 or Sandholt on Laugavegur from 07:30, then coffee at Mokka from 9:00.
Reserve Grillmarkaðurinn, Fiskmarkaðurinn or Snaps through Dineout, and remember Matur og Drykkur is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several sites could not be read: Sky Lagoon (JavaScript loading screen only), Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur and Kolaportið (HTTP 429), Sægreifinn, Kaffi Vínyl and junglebar.is (domains did not resolve), and Hlemmur Mathöll (certificate error); none of these failures is evidence of closure. Grandi Mathöll, the Botanic Garden, Þingvellir, the Maritime Museum and Árbær Open Air Museum were left out because their pages showed no exact address or hours. Dill and the Settlement Exhibition did not publish readable hours; Reykjavík Art Museum showed no exhibition dates; Hallgrímskirkja's readable hours date from its May 2026 summer notice and may differ in winter. Sandholt, Mokka, Reykjavík Roasters, Whales of Iceland and Slippbarinn showed current hours but no 2026-dated content.
